title: Neobiani Royal-Style Grilled Beef
shortDescription: Broad, thin pieces of tenderized beef are marinated with pear, soy sauce, garlic, scallion, sesame, and black pepper, then grilled quickly and cut for serving.
culturalContext: Neobiani is commonly described as a broad, tenderized, marinated beef preparation associated with Korean court-style cooking and later formal presentations. Historical and royal-cuisine claims require specialist review; this draft focuses on the practical cut, marinade, and grill method.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Chef’s knife and separate raw-meat cutting board
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill

ingredients.item: boneless beef short rib, ribeye, or sirloin
ingredients.preparation: cut across the grain into broad 6 mm / 1/4-inch slices and lightly pounded

mixOrder: Dissolve brown sugar in soy sauce
Stir in grated pear and onion
Add garlic, scallions, sesame oil, sesame seeds, black pepper, and optional rice syrup
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Covered nonreactive bowl or food-safe zip bag set in a rimmed tray
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 12 hours in this pear-forward draft; extended fruit-enzyme exposure can make thin beef surfaces mushy.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve 60 ml / 1/4 cup marinade in a clean covered bowl before adding beef if a cooked serving glaze is desired.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard all marinade that touched raw beef; do not brush it onto cooked meat. Any separately reserved clean portion may be boiled in a saucepan before service.
substitutions: Asian pear may replace Korean pear.
Use verified gluten-free tamari only after checking the label.
allergenNotes: wheat/gluten unless certified alternatives are used

instructions.heading: Slice and tenderize
instructions.action: Keep beef cold. Cut across the grain into broad 6 mm / 1/4-inch slices, cover with parchment, and pound lightly to an even 4 mm / 3/16-inch thickness without tearing.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pieces are broad, even, and flexible with visible surface scoring from the mallet.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not rinse raw beef; use a dedicated board and wash hands and tools after contact.

instructions.heading: Mix and reserve marinade
instructions.action: Dissolve sugar in soy sauce, then add pear, onion, garlic, scallions, sesame oil, sesame seeds, pepper, and optional rice syrup. Reserve 60 ml / 1/4 cup in a clean bowl before raw contact.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sugar is dissolved and the marinade is evenly pulpy.
instructions.safetyNote: Label and refrigerate the clean reserve immediately; never confuse it with raw-contact marinade.

instructions.heading: Marinate cold
instructions.action: Coat beef thoroughly in the remaining marinade, cover, set over a rimmed tray, and refrigerate 2 to 8 hours.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every surface has a thin even coating and the beef remains cold.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate on the counter; discard all marinade that touched raw beef.

instructions.heading: Preheat safely
instructions.action: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill to medium-high. Establish separate raw and cooked utensil zones.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Grates are hot, scrubbed, and lightly oiled; clean platter and tongs are ready.
instructions.safetyNote: Never use charcoal, propane, or other fuel-burning grills indoors or in enclosed spaces.

instructions.heading: Grill in batches
instructions.action: Lift beef from marinade, allowing excess to drip back into the raw container. Grill without crowding, about 2 to 3 minutes per side, moving pieces away from flare-ups.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Edges caramelize, surfaces brown, and the center remains moist without raw-looking patches.
instructions.safetyNote: Use raw tongs until the final turn, then switch to clean tongs; sugary marinade can flare and burn.

instructions.heading: Verify and rest
instructions.action: Check representative pieces in the thickest portion with a calibrated thermometer. Move beef to a clean platter only after it reaches 145°F / 63°C, then rest 3 minutes. If using the clean reserve, boil it before spooning lightly over the rested beef.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Beef is browned, thermometer-verified, and juices settle during the rest.
instructions.safetyNote: Thin pieces are difficult to probe; stack two representative pieces if needed without understating the required temperature.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill with working ventilation. Preheat to medium-high, oil lightly, create raw and cooked zones, and keep a clean thermometer, tongs, and platter ready.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion, followed by a 3-minute rest
visualDonenessCues: Broad slices are caramelized at the edges
Representative thick portions reach 145°F / 63°C before a 3-minute rest
foodSafetyNotes: Do not rinse raw beef and prevent raw juices from contacting ready-to-eat foods.
Marinate only under refrigeration at or below 40°F / 4°C.
Reserve any serving sauce before raw contact and discard raw-contact marinade.
Use separate raw and cooked utensils and a clean platter.
Verify 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion and rest 3 minutes.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify all packaged labels and protect the grill and utensils from allergen cross-contact.

substitutions: Boneless ribeye or sirloin may replace short-rib meat when sliced and pounded evenly.
Use only verified gluten-free tamari for a gluten-free adaptation.
ingredientSourcing: Ask for boneless short-rib meat or well-marbled beef that can be cut into broad slices.
Choose a fragrant ripe Korean or Asian pear without bruised flesh.
makeAhead: Mix marinade up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate. Slice and marinate beef no more than 8 hours before cooking under this draft.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef in a shallow airtight container within 2 hours and use within 4 days, consistent with general cooked-leftover guidance pending review.
reheating: Reheat once in a covered skillet with a spoonful of water until steaming, then uncover briefly; avoid repeated cooling and reheating.
leftovers: Slice properly refrigerated leftovers for a rice bowl or lettuce wrap within the approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Cut broad pieces into bite-size sections after resting
Serve with rice, ssam greens, and a separately portioned sauce

faq.question: Why pound the beef?
faq.answer: Gentle pounding evens the thickness, broadens the pieces, and helps them cook quickly without tearing.

faq.question: Can raw marinade become sauce?
faq.answer: Discard raw-contact marinade. Reserve a portion before adding beef and boil that clean reserve before serving if desired.
